claims.explanation: WZ-4002 is a dual EGFR/ERBB2 kinase inhibitor, so selective killing is best explained by dependence on EGFR/ERBB2 signaling, especially EGFR mutation/amplification or high EGFR/ERBB2 expression. The sensitive set is enriched for lung and upper aerodigestive squamous/NSCLC lines with EGFR pathway alterations, while resistant lines often have BRAF/NRAS/MAP2K1 or PTEN/PIK3CA alterations that bypass EGFR/ERBB2 or activate downstream MAPK/PI3K independently. Co-occurring ARID1A, TP53, or other mutations are likely passenger/context features rather than the primary selectivity determinant.

features.basis: EGFR kinase-domain mutations sensitize to EGFR inhibitors; HCC4006 is EGFR-mutant and selectively killed
EGFR/ERBB2 inhibitor requires EGFR pathway dependence; high EGFR expression predicts response
WZ-4002 directly targets ERBB2; ERBB2-driven lines should be sensitive
ERBB2 kinase-domain mutations can be sensitive to ERBB2 inhibitors
BRAF-mutant melanoma/colorectal lines are largely in the resistant set, suggesting MAPK bypass
NRAS mutations activate MAPK independently of EGFR/ERBB2 and appear in resistant lines
MAP2K1 mutation can bypass upstream EGFR/ERBB2 inhibition; NCIH1437 is resistant
PTEN loss activates PI3K/AKT downstream of EGFR and is enriched in resistant lines
PIK3CA mutation can drive PI3K signaling independent of EGFR/ERBB2; seen in resistant lines
NF1 loss activates RAS/MAPK and is common in resistant lines
MET alteration can bypass EGFR/ERBB2 dependence; HGC27 and 8305C are resistant
ARID1A mutations appear in several sensitive lines but mechanism is unclear and likely context-dependent
